text: A point representation assigns to every commutative R-algebra A an action of Hom_R-alg(H,A), with convolution multiplication, on A⊗V, naturally in A. This is [Milne VIII§2’s definition](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=112), with tensor factors reversed. The source quantifies over an algebra universe containing R, H and V, so universal points remain available without finite-generation or freeness assumptions. Checks pass: [action_naturality](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Comodule/Basic.lean#L122), [ofComodule_toComodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Comodule/Basic.lean#L693).
Checks naturality in the value algebra.
Checks that every such natural action is recovered from its coaction.

This exposes the component of a natural representation at A as a homomorphism into Aut_A(A⊗V), the group in [Milne VIII§2](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=112). The equality transport only identifies the functor’s packaged value with that concrete group; it does not change the automorphism or impose a basis. Checks pass: [action_def](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Comodule/Basic.lean#L94), [action_naturality](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Comodule/Basic.lean#L122).
Identifies the component and its equality transport.
Checks the exposed components retain naturality.

The concrete action is the natural-transformation component followed by the canonical identification of its codomain with Aut_A(A⊗V). This is the componentwise interpretation of [Milne’s natural representation](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=112). Lean’s equality map changes the packaging of an equal object, not the resulting action or its multiplication order. Checks pass: [action_naturality](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Comodule/Basic.lean#L122), [action_mapPoints_one_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Comodule/Basic.lean#L135).
Checks the concrete wrapper is compatible with algebra maps.
Checks its elementwise naturality on generating tensors.

Two natural representations coincide if their automorphisms agree for every value algebra and every point. This compares the entire natural family in [Milne VIII§2](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=112), rather than only base-field points. Cancelling the codomain identification reduces the proof to equality of group homomorphisms and then natural-transformation components. Checks pass: [ofComodule_toComodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Comodule/Basic.lean#L693).
Uses this extensionality principle to recover the whole original natural representation.

For an algebra map φ:A→B, extending the automorphism attached to x equals the automorphism attached to φ∘x. This is exactly the [naturality square in Milne VIII§2](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=112). Both sides act on B⊗V; extension of automorphisms is defined without assuming φ or the tensor comparison injective. Checks pass: [action_mapPoints_one_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Comodule/Basic.lean#L135), [mapScalarExtensionAutomorphisms_apply_scalarExtensionMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/ScalarExtension.lean#L148).
Evaluates the naturality square on 1⊗v.
Checks how extended automorphisms intertwine the tensor comparison.

The action at the transported point φ∘x on 1⊗v is obtained by applying φ⊗id to the original action on 1⊗v. This is the generating-vector form of [Milne’s naturality square](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=120). Since these vectors generate after extending scalars, no injectivity or flatness hypothesis is needed. Checks pass: [action_naturality](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Comodule/Basic.lean#L122), [scalarExtensionMap_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/ScalarExtension.lean#L71).
Supplies the full naturality identity.
Checks the comparison carries 1⊗v to 1⊗v.

A right coaction ρ(v)=Σv₀⊗v₁ gives the action a⊗v↦Σa·x(v₁)⊗v₀. This is [Milne VIII§6, equation (78)](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=120), after swapping his scalar-extension factors. The Hopf point group provides inverse automorphisms, and compatibility with coefficient-algebra maps supplies naturality for arbitrary modules over a commutative ring. Checks pass: [ofComodule_action_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Comodule/Basic.lean#L232), [toComodule_ofComodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Comodule/Basic.lean#L668).
Checks the induced action on pure tensors.
Recovering the coaction returns the supplied structure.

The action evaluates x on the coefficient leg of ρ(v), swaps the factors, and multiplies the scalar factor by a. This yields Σa·x(v₁)⊗v₀, agreeing with [Milne’s formula (78)](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=120). Tensor notation represents a linear map, so it requires neither a chosen decomposition nor a basis. Checks pass: [ofComodule_action_val_eq_endOfPoint](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Comodule/Basic.lean#L245), [ofComodule_action_universal_one_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Comodule/Basic.lean#L252).
Identifies the underlying linear map with the native point action.
Checks evaluation at the universal point.

Forgetting invertibility from the induced action gives exactly the coefficient-evaluation endomorphism endOfPoint. Thus the passage from [Milne’s representation formula](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=120) to a group-valued natural transformation preserves the actual linear action. The source cancels the functor-object identifications and the equivalence between invertible endomorphisms and linear automorphisms. Checks pass: [ofComodule_action_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Comodule/Basic.lean#L232), [ofComodule_action_universal_one_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Comodule/Basic.lean#L252).
Checks the same map on every pure tensor.
Checks its universal-point specialization.

At the universal point, evaluation leaves every coefficient unchanged, so the action on 1⊗v is the flipped coaction. This is [Milne VIII§6’s universal-element construction](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=119). The displayed ULift is an isomorphic copy of H in a sufficiently large universe; it neither extends scalars mathematically nor changes coefficients. Checks pass: [ofComodule_action_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Comodule/Basic.lean#L232), [toComodule_ofComodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Comodule/Basic.lean#L668).
Specializes the general coefficient-evaluation formula.
Checks that removing the lift and flipping back recovers the coaction.

Evaluating the natural action at the universal H-point and flipping H⊗V to V⊗H recovers a right coaction, as in [Milne VIII§6](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=119). Naturality at the counit proves the counit law; the convolution product of the two tensor inclusions proves coassociativity. No basis, flatness or finiteness is assumed. Checks pass: [toComodule_coact_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Comodule/Basic.lean#L655), [ofComodule_toComodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Comodule/Basic.lean#L693).
Exposes the recovered coaction and universe identifications.
The recovered coaction induces the original natural action.

The recovered coaction first acts at the universal point on 1⊗v, removes the universe lift from H, and swaps factors to land in V⊗H. This spells out [Milne’s universal-element recovery](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=119). The lifts are canonical algebra equivalences; the formula introduces no embedding or choice of generators. Checks pass: [toComodule_ofComodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Comodule/Basic.lean#L668), [ofComodule_toComodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Comodule/Basic.lean#L693).
Checks recovery on a coaction-induced representation.
Checks the converse recovery on an arbitrary natural action.

Starting with a coaction, forming its point action and recovering at the universal point returns that same coaction. Universal evaluation is the identity on coefficients, and the two tensor flips cancel. This verifies one direction of [Milne VIII Proposition 6.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=119) for arbitrary modules, with no freeness assumption. Checks pass: [ofComodule_action_universal_one_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Comodule/Basic.lean#L252), [toComodule_coact_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Comodule/Basic.lean#L655).
Computes the forward action at the universal point.
Computes the recovery operation.

Recovering the coaction and rebuilding the action returns the entire original natural representation. The actions first agree at the universal point; naturality along each x:H→A then gives agreement everywhere. This is the general, basis-free proof of [Milne VIII Proposition 6.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=120), not merely a comparison of base-valued points. Checks pass: [action_naturality](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Comodule/Basic.lean#L122), [ofComodule_action_universal_one_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Comodule/Basic.lean#L252).
Propagates agreement from the universal point to every value algebra.
Checks the universal-point calculation used in reconstruction.

This is Aut_A(A⊗_R V), encoded as units of the endomorphism ring: a unit stores an endomorphism and a two-sided inverse. It is the group Aut_V(A) of [Milne VIII§2](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=112), with scalar factors written first. V may be arbitrary; representability by an affine scheme is not asserted. Checks pass: [val_mapScalarExtensionAutomorphisms](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/ScalarExtension.lean#L128), [mapScalarExtensionAutomorphisms_id](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/ScalarExtension.lean#L186).
Checks how the underlying endomorphism changes with the value algebra.
Checks identity base change of these groups.

The canonical comparison A⊗V→B⊗V sends a⊗v to φ(a)⊗v. This is the tensor-product map supplied by the [universal property, Stacks 10.12.2](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00CV). It is R-linear and φ-semilinear on the scalar factor; it need not be injective, and the construction uses no flatness assumption. Checks pass: [scalarExtensionMap_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/ScalarExtension.lean#L71), [scalarExtensionMap_smul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/ScalarExtension.lean#L110).
Checks the pure-tensor formula.
Checks semilinearity for the algebra map.

Tensoring φ:A→B with the identity of V sends precisely a⊗v to φ(a)⊗v. The formula agrees with the [tensor universal property](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00CV) and preserves factor order. It computes the canonical R-linear comparison itself; calling the input a pure tensor does not imply that every tensor is pure. Checks pass: [scalarExtensionMap_eq_map](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/ScalarExtension.lean#L78), [scalarExtensionMap_smul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/ScalarExtension.lean#L110).
Identifies the full map with φ⊗id.
Checks compatibility with the value-algebra scalar action.

The comparison is exactly φ⊗id_V, not a different map between the same tensor products. Equality follows by testing pure tensors, which generate additively, as in [Stacks 10.12.2](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00CV). This identifies both the scalar leg and the unchanged module leg without requiring a basis or an injective coefficient map. Checks pass: [scalarExtensionMap_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/ScalarExtension.lean#L71), [scalarExtensionMap_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/ScalarExtension.lean#L101).
Checks equality on the generating pure tensors.
Checks the resulting maps compose in the expected direction.

An A-linear automorphism extends to B⊗V by b⊗v↦b·(φ⊗id)(g(1⊗v)). The [scalar-extension universal property, Stacks 10.14.3](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05G3), supplies this map; extending g⁻¹ supplies its inverse. The source packages preservation of composition as a group homomorphism, without requiring faithful scalar extension or a finite free module. Checks pass: [mapScalarExtensionAutomorphisms_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/ScalarExtension.lean#L138), [mapScalarExtensionAutomorphisms_apply_scalarExtensionMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/ScalarExtension.lean#L148).
Checks the extended automorphism on pure tensors.
Checks the defining intertwining square.

The underlying endomorphism of an extended automorphism is the ordinary scalar extension of its underlying endomorphism. This follows because the construction applies a ring homomorphism to units, retaining the extended inverse. It agrees with the [base-change construction characterized by Stacks 10.14.3](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05G3); forgetting invertibility does not alter the linear map. Checks pass: [mapScalarExtensionAutomorphisms_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/ScalarExtension.lean#L138), [mapScalarExtensionAutomorphisms_apply_scalarExtensionMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/ScalarExtension.lean#L148).
Computes that underlying endomorphism on pure tensors.
Checks its defining comparison square.

Extending g commutes with the comparison j=φ⊗id: the identity is g_B(j(x))=j(g(x)). This is the defining [scalar-extension square from the tensor universal property](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05G3). It holds for every x, even when j has a kernel; invertibility of g does not imply injectivity of j. Checks pass: [mapScalarExtensionAutomorphisms_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/ScalarExtension.lean#L138), [eq_mapScalarExtensionAutomorphisms_of_apply_scalarExtensionMap_eq](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/ScalarExtension.lean#L159).
Checks the extended map on arbitrary target pure tensors.
Checks that the square characterizes the extension.

A B-linear automorphism satisfying the comparison square must be the extension of g. Although j:A⊗V→B⊗V need not be surjective, its image contains every 1⊗v and therefore generates over B. The uniqueness is exactly the [extension property of Stacks 10.14.3](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05G3), with no cancellation or flatness assumption. Checks pass: [mapScalarExtensionAutomorphisms_apply_scalarExtensionMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/ScalarExtension.lean#L148), [mapScalarExtensionAutomorphisms_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/ScalarExtension.lean#L138).
The constructed extension satisfies the required square.
Checks the formula forced on target generators.

Extending an automorphism along the identity algebra map returns the same automorphism. The defining square has identity comparison, so uniqueness of [scalar extension](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05G3) identifies the underlying endomorphisms; equality of units then identifies the automorphisms. This is the identity law needed for the value-algebra functor, for arbitrary V. Checks pass: [scalarExtensionMap_id](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/ScalarExtension.lean#L93), [mapScalarExtensionAutomorphisms_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/ScalarExtension.lean#L138).
The comparison for an identity algebra map is identity.
Checks the extension formula on pure tensors.

Extending along A→B→C equals extension along the composite A→C. Both endomorphisms satisfy the same tensor-comparison square, hence agree by the [scalar-extension universal property](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05G3). Categorical composition runs first A→B and then B→C; the source’s equation preserves that order and requires no flatness. Checks pass: [scalarExtensionMap_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/ScalarExtension.lean#L101), [mapScalarExtensionAutomorphisms_apply_scalarExtensionMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/ScalarExtension.lean#L148).
Checks composition of the canonical tensor comparisons.
Checks the square used to identify both extensions.

The assignments A↦Aut_A(A⊗V) and φ↦extension of automorphisms form the group-valued functor Aut_V of [Milne VIII§2](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=112). The source supplies its identity and composition laws explicitly. It fixes V throughout; this construction by itself neither represents the functor by a scheme nor makes automorphisms covariant in arbitrary module maps. Checks pass: [mapScalarExtensionAutomorphisms_id](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/ScalarExtension.lean#L186), [mapScalarExtensionAutomorphisms_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/ScalarExtension.lean#L195).
Checks the functor identity law.
Checks the functor composition law.

Adding the same finite extended nonnegative value on the left preserves and reflects non-strict order: a+b≤a+c exactly when b≤c. The compared values may be infinite, and the common summand may be zero. Infinity cannot serve as the common summand, since it makes both sums equal regardless of the original comparison. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Operations.lean#L121).

A finite common summand can be cancelled from the right of a non-strict inequality: b+a≤c+a exactly when b≤c. Neither b nor c is required finite. The finiteness condition concerns only the shared summand; adding infinity would erase the distinction between unequal inputs because every resulting sum is infinity. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Operations.lean#L124).

Adding a finite common summand on the right preserves and reflects strict order: b+a<c+a exactly when b<c. The upper value c may be infinity. The common summand must be finite; if it were infinity, both sums would be infinity, so even 1<2 would lose its strictness after addition. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Operations.lean#L130).

From a<b and c≤d one obtains a+c<b+d when c is finite. No finiteness assumption is needed on b or d; if either is infinite, the upper sum is infinite while the lower sum remains finite. The guard on c prevents both sums from becoming infinity and destroying the strict inequality. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Operations.lean#L136).

Adding a finite value a and then subtracting it recovers the other summand: (a+b)−a=b. Subtraction is truncated at zero, but no truncation loss occurs because a≤a+b. The other summand may be infinity. The finite guard matters: (∞+1)−∞ is zero under Lean’s convention, not one. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Operations.lean#L341).

For finite b, subtracting b from a+b recovers a, even when a is infinity. This uses truncated nonnegative subtraction, with the added term guaranteeing that subtraction does not go below zero. Allowing b to be infinity would fail: for a=1, the expression (1+∞)−∞ is zero rather than one. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Operations.lean#L344).

If a is finite and a+b≤c, then b≤c−a. The subtraction is truncated, but the premise already ensures a≤c, so this recovers the familiar subtraction of a common term. The values b and c may be infinite. Without finiteness, ∞+1≤∞ would incorrectly imply 1≤∞−∞=0. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Operations.lean#L377).

Adding a nonzero extended nonnegative value to a finite one strictly increases it: a<a+b. The added value b may itself be infinity, in which case the result is infinity and still exceeds finite a. Both restrictions are meaningful: adding zero changes nothing, while no sum can strictly exceed an already infinite a. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Operations.lean#L142).

Subtracting any nonzero extended nonnegative value from a positive finite value strictly decreases it. There is no requirement that the subtrahend be smaller or finite: if it is at least the original value, truncated subtraction gives zero, still strictly smaller. The original value must exclude zero and infinity for this general claim. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Operations.lean#L398).

Multiplication distributes over truncated subtraction, (a−b)·c=a·c−b·c, provided c is finite whenever 0<b<a. No restriction on c is needed when b=0 or a≤b. The conditional guard is necessary: with a=2,b=1,c=∞, the left side is infinity but the right side is ∞−∞=0. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Operations.lean#L415).

A positive finite extended nonnegative value divided by itself equals one. Both exclusions matter because this arithmetic defines 0/0=0 and ∞/∞=0. Thus the familiar self-division identity applies on the ordinary positive finite domain, while the two endpoint self-quotients have a different explicitly defined value. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L512).

Dividing b by a positive finite a and then multiplying by a recovers b. The numerator b may be zero or infinity; only the cancelled denominator is restricted. With a=0 or a=∞, the resulting product is zero under the endpoint conventions, so it would fail to recover a nonzero numerator. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L177).

Multiplying a quotient b/a on the left by its positive finite denominator a gives b. This also holds for an infinite numerator. The restrictions apply to a alone: a zero or infinite denominator makes the product zero, so unrestricted cancellation would fail whenever b is nonzero. Commutativity gives the corresponding right-multiplication version. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L189).

A positive finite common factor cancels from numerator and denominator: (c·a)/(c·b)=a/b. The values a and b themselves may be zero or infinity, so the identity includes totalized endpoint quotients. The common factor must remain nonzero and finite; otherwise multiplying both inputs can erase distinctions needed to preserve their quotient. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L265).

The inequality a·(b/a)≤b holds for all extended nonnegative values without denominator restrictions. For positive finite a, cancellation gives equality. At a=0 or a=∞, the product is zero, so the inequality still holds and is strict when b is positive. This weaker statement remains valid where unrestricted cancellation would fail. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L515).

An extended nonnegative quotient is nonzero exactly when its numerator is nonzero and its denominator is finite. The denominator may be zero: a nonzero numerator divided by zero gives infinity, which is nonzero. An infinite denominator always gives zero. Thus “finite denominator” here must not be replaced by “nonzero denominator.” Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L551).

A nonzero extended nonnegative numerator divided by a finite denominator has a strictly positive quotient. Finiteness does not require the denominator to be nonzero: division by zero produces infinity for a nonzero numerator. The numerator may also be infinity. Positivity describes the extended order and does not assert that the quotient is finite. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L227).

Cross multiplication gives a/b≤c exactly when a≤c·b, provided (b,c) is neither (0,∞) nor (∞,0). Positive finite denominators satisfy these conditions automatically. The excluded pairs matter because their product c·b is zero, although a/b≤c holds for every numerator; a positive numerator therefore breaks the equivalence. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L384).

The strict comparison c/b<a is equivalent to c<a·b when numerator c and denominator b are not both zero and not both infinity. Individual endpoint values are allowed. If both are zero or both infinity, c/b=0; choosing a=1 makes the quotient comparison true while the cross-multiplied strict comparison is false. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L422).

The inequality a≤c/b is equivalent to a·b≤c when c and b are not both zero and not both infinity. This extends ordinary cross multiplication beyond positive finite denominators. The exclusions are essential: with a=1 and either forbidden pair, the quotient is zero, so the left inequality fails while the product inequality holds. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L370).

For a fixed monomial order, G lies in I and its leading terms generate the same ideal as all leading terms of I. Leading terms include coefficients. This extends the usual field definition to commutative semirings, allowing infinite G and infinitely many variables; existence of division remainders separately requires ring coefficients and invertible nonzero leading coefficients. See [Godsil, More Linear Algebra, §1.8, pp.13–14](https://www.math.uwaterloo.ca/~cgodsil/quagmire/pdfs/LA.pdf). Native Checks pass: [Removing zero preserves the basis](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/RingTheory/MvPolynomial/Groebner.lean#L207), [A given remainder vanishes exactly on the ideal](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/RingTheory/MvPolynomial/Groebner.lean#L303), [Unit leading coefficients give a unique remainder](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/RingTheory/MvPolynomial/Groebner.lean#L323).

For a finitely generated algebra A over any field with irreducible spectrum, every prime p satisfies ht(p)+dim(A/p)=dim(A). Height counts prime-chain lengths below p; dim(A/p) is the dimension of its closed locus. Nilpotents are allowed: quotienting by the nilradical preserves both quantities. These dimensions are finite, despite Lean’s extended-number codomains. See [Stacks, Lemma10.116.3 (00P1)](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00P1). Native Checks pass: [Maximal ideals in n-variable polynomial rings have height n](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/RingTheory/KrullDimension/FiniteType.lean#L268), [Maximal primes have full height](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/RingTheory/KrullDimension/FiniteType.lean#L452), [Reduction preserves prime heights](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/RingTheory/KrullDimension/Quotient.lean#L168), [Reduction preserves dimension](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/RingTheory/KrullDimension/Quotient.lean#L115).
